title: Cleavers infusion for pelvic lymphatic support
subtitle: A cold-infused tea of fresh Galium aparine for lymphatic and pelvic tissue health
excerpt: Cleavers infusion is a cold extract of fresh Galium aparine herb, steeped overnight in cold water and drunk first thing in the morning. Long used in European herbal tradition as a lymphatic herb for pelvic tissue health, skin congestion, and swollen glands. The cold preparation preserves the mucilaginous constituents that make it effective. Best prepared in spring when the plant is fresh and young.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), cleavers entry, Botanical.com. Nicholas Culpeper, Complete Herbal (1653), goosegrass entry, public domain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best prepared fresh from plant. Cold-steep overnight; do not use the previous day's infusion.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb traditionally used to support the flow and clearance of the lymphatic system, the network of vessels and nodes that drain fluid from tissues and carry immune cells. Cleavers is one of the most widely used lymphatic herbs in European herbal practice.

content.text: Cleavers infusion is a cold-water extract of fresh Galium aparine, steeped overnight in a jar and drunk as the first drink of the day. A traditional

, used in European herbal practice for swollen pelvic or inguinal lymph nodes, tissue congestion, and the kind of generalised sluggishness that traditional herbalists comes with poor lymphatic flow. The cold infusion method is deliberate: heat destroys the gel-rich active compounds responsible for much of the action. The taste is mild, vegetal, and faintly sweet. A spring herb, picked young and used fresh, before the plant goes to seed.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Rinse two large handfuls of fresh cleavers under cold water. Loosely pack into a large clean jar.
Pour 500 ml of cold water over the herb. Cover and refrigerate overnight (8 hours minimum).
Strain through a fine strainer into a glass. Drink 200 to 250 ml as the first drink of the day, before breakfast. The remainder can be drunk throughout the morning.
One jar per day, drunk in the morning, for 2 to 4 weeks during spring. Traditionally used as a cleansing spring remedy before the plant goes to seed.
Use the steeped liquid the morning after preparation. Do not keep for more than 24 hours.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you cannot find or grow fresh cleavers, the dried herb is not an adequate substitute for this preparation. See a doctor for any lymph node swelling that is hard, enlarging, or comes with fever, night sweats, or weight loss.
